canal-h1.title: 大运河
trans: The Sui Dynasty emperor wanted to build a very long canal.
At that time, travel between north and south was very difficult.
One journey took many days.
Many people worked together and built the Grand Canal.
The work was hard and took many years.
The Grand Canal goes from north to south — very, very long.
Merchants sailed boats on the Canal to transport goods.
Rice from the south could now be sent north.
Over time many cities grew up along the canal.
Today, the Canal still exists and people are still using it.

canal2-h1.title: 坐船游玩
trans: During summer holiday, Dad took me for a boat ride.
We reached the river in the morning; the boat was big.
The boat moved slowly on the water — very comfortable.
A breeze came across and it was not hot at all.
I saw many fish and birds.
Fish swam in the water and birds flew in the sky.
Mum prepared a delicious lunch for us.
On the boat we ate and talked at the same time.
In the evening the boat came back.
That day I had so much fun — very unforgettable.

dongzhou2-h1.title: 猫和老鼠

sents.mn: the back; the rear; the last bit

trans: There was a cat and a mouse.
They lived in a very big house.
The cat wanted to eat the mouse; the mouse ran very fast.
The mouse ran through the door and the cat followed behind.
The mouse ran to the mountain and the cat couldn't catch it.
The cat was too tired and sat at the foot of the mountain without moving.
On the mountain the mouse found many delicious things.
There was water there, and many flowers too.
The cat went home, and the mouse stayed on the mountain.
It said: "This is great — I'm not going back down!"

han-h1.title: 丝绸之路
trans: In the Han dynasty, China and the lands to the west had little contact.
Han Dynasty people walked very far towards the west.
The road was long; one journey took many months.
They carried Chinese silk to trade.
Western merchants brought gold and many good things.
They also brought new fruits and horses.
People on both sides got to know each other through this road.
Chinese paper and writing travelled out along this road too.
Later, people called this road the Silk Road.
The Silk Road connected China and the world together.

han2-h1.title: 我的小猫
trans: I have a little cat named Little White.
It is white, with big eyes.
It wakes me up every morning.
After I get up, I feed it first.
It loves to eat fish and also loves to play with a ball.
Sometimes it climbs onto my school bag to sleep.
When I leave for school, it watches me from the doorway.
When I come home, it runs over to me.
At night it sleeps beside my bed.
I love my little cat very much; it is my best friend.

konfucius-h1.title: 孔子的学生

sents.mn: to know; to become aware of

trans: More than two thousand years ago there was a teacher in China called Confucius.
Confucius was a good teacher.
He had many students.
Some of his students were older, some younger.
They read together and talked together.
He said: "Studying every day is very good."
He also said: "If you do not know, ask — that is good."
The students loved Confucius.
After he died, his students wrote his words down.
Today, Chinese people all remember Confucius's words.

ming-h1.title: 郑和下西洋
trans: Ming Dynasty's Zheng He led a gigantic fleet and set sail.
His fleet had more than three hundred large ships.
They reached Southeast Asia, India, Arabia, and even Africa.
They brought Chinese silk, porcelain, and tea.
Zheng He's voyages showed China's greatness and friendship.

ming2-h1.title: 奇妙的发现
trans: During the Ming Dynasty, Li Shizhen spent nearly 30 years writing the Compendium of Materia Medica.
This book recorded nearly 2,000 kinds of plants and medicines — extremely precious.
Xu Xiake traveled all over China's famous mountains and rivers, recording geographic explorations.
The spirit of these scientists inspired generation after generation of explorers.
The spirit of science is to explore courageously, never stopping.

paper-h1.title: 纸的故事
trans: Before, people wrote on bamboo sticks — very heavy.
One book took a great deal of bamboo — one person could not carry it.
During the Eastern Han, Cai Lun discovered he could make paper from tree bark.
He used tree bark, old cloth and water to make paper.
Paper is light and also cheap.
With paper, people could write many characters.
Students could carry books to school, and teachers could write out lessons.
Later, paper travelled from China to other countries.
Many people around the world began writing on paper.
Cai Lun's invention changed China and the world.

paper2-h1.title: 书里的世界
trans: My favourite thing is books.
There are many books in my room.
Books contain many interesting stories.
Some books are about things from long ago.
Some are about the animals of the sky and the water.
When I read books, I can go to faraway places.
Mum said: "Reading makes you smarter."
She also said I can ask her about any character I do not know.
I read every evening.
I have already read many books; I want to read even more.

print-h1.title: 印书的故事
trans: During the Five Dynasties, people began printing books by carving wood.
They carved many characters on a block of wood, then applied ink.
This way, many books could be printed very quickly.
Books became cheap and more people could read.
This invention was an important step in the history of printing.

print2-h1.title: 图书馆的一天
trans: Today the teacher took us to the library.
The library has thousands and thousands of books.
I found a story book about ancient China.
I read for two hours in the library and forgot about time.
I borrowed three books to take home, eager to finish reading them.

qin-h1.title: 万里长城
trans: Qin Shi Huang was China's first great king.
He made the characters of China all the same.
People often came from the north, so he wanted very much to do one thing.
He wanted to build a very large Great Wall.
Many people came to do this work.
They worked from morning to night, and it was very hard.
The Great Wall is on the mountains, very long.
It is more than twenty thousand li long, which is why it is called the Ten-Thousand-Li Great Wall.
More than two thousand years have passed, and the Great Wall is still there.
Today, people can still see it.

qin2-h1.title: 爬山的孩子
trans: Today, we went to climb the mountain.
The weather was fine in the morning, and we left at eight.
The mountain was very big; we walked for a long time.
There were many trees along the way, and small birds too.
I was tired and said: "I don't want to walk anymore."
I sat down and drank some water.
A friend said: "Almost there! Keep going!"
I thought about it, stood up and walked on.
We reached the top and happily shouted: "We did it!"
Looking down from the mountain, home looked very, very small.

qing-h1.title: 康熙皇帝
trans: The Qing Dynasty's Emperor Kangxi ruled China for 61 years.
He was an extremely hardworking emperor.
He personally studied mathematics, music, and Western science.
Under his rule, China's territory reached its greatest extent.
He is regarded as one of the greatest emperors in Chinese history.

qing2-h1.title: 故宫里的秘密
trans: Beijing's Forbidden City is the world's largest ancient palace complex.
It was built by a Ming Dynasty emperor and has more than 9,000 rooms.
The emperor received hundreds of officials in the Hall of Supreme Harmony and handled state affairs.
The artworks and treasures in the palace showed the glorious achievements of ancient China.
Today, the Palace Museum receives millions of visitors every year.

reform-h1.title: 改变的时代
trans: In the late Qing Dynasty, China faced enormous pressure from the West.
Young reformers hoped to learn Western science and technology.
Some officials believed China needed to establish modern schools and armies.
The path of reform was very difficult, but people did not give up.
The spirit of this era influenced China's later historical development.

reform2-h1.title: 变化中的上海
trans: At the end of the 19th century, Shanghai developed into China's most modern city.
Merchants from around the world lived there, bringing new ideas and technology.
New-style schools, newspapers, and factories rapidly developed in Shanghai.
Traditional Chinese culture and Western modern civilization collided here.
Shanghai's transformation reflected all of China's struggle and effort in modernization.

republic-h1.title: 新中国的梦
trans: Sun Yat-sen put forward the ideals of democracy, civil rights, and people's livelihood.
He believed the Chinese people had the ability to build a modern state.
After years of effort, the Republic of China was established in 1912.
The new government established a modern education system.
Although the road was full of challenges, people were full of hope for the future.

republic2-h1.title: 新时代的年轻人
trans: During the Republic era, China produced a generation of young people full of ideals.
They received new-style education, studying science, democracy, and modern culture.
Many went abroad to study and returned to contribute to China's development.
They created new literature, researched new science, and pushed society forward.
They believed education and knowledge were the key to changing the nation's destiny.

rider-h1.title: 草原骑手
trans: The Khitan people of the Liao Dynasty lived on the grasslands of northern China.
They were excellent horse riders, riding every day.
They created their own script and laws.
Liao and Song traded and exchanged various goods.
Khitan culture influenced northern China for a long time.

rider2-h1.title: 草原上的风
trans: On the northern grasslands, the wind blows very strongly.
Khitan children galloped on horseback across the grasslands.
They studied archery and riding, preparing for the future.
Life on the grasslands was difficult but full of freedom.
They loved their own land and culture.

sanguo-h1.title: 诸葛亮的智慧

sents.mn: to think (i.e. to take it to be true that ...) (Usually there is an implication that the notion is mistaken – except when expressing one's own current opinion.)

trans: During the Three Kingdoms period, China had three kingdoms.
The three kingdoms fought each other again and again.
Zhuge Liang was a person of great wisdom.
He was good at finding a way, and good at reading the weather.
He helped Liu Bei win many battles.
One time he used a clever plan and all the enemies ran away.
Another time, he sat alone on the city wall reading.
The enemy saw him, thought the city was full of soldiers, and left.
He served his kingdom until he was very old.
His story still moves people today.

sanguo2-h1.title: 好朋友的力量
trans: I have three very good friends.
We are at the same school and in the same class.
We study, eat, and play together.
Sometimes we disagree, but we make up quickly.
One time I got sick and my friends came to visit.
They brought food and books and kept me company.
One friend told me what had been happening at school.
I was so glad to hear it that I forgot I was ill.
The next day I wanted to go back to school.
The power of good friends made me get well very quickly.

scholar-h1.title: 勤学的年轻人
trans: Jin Dynasty young people worked hard to learn Chinese characters.
They went to school to read books, practicing writing every day.
If you mastered Chinese characters, you could become an official or merchant.
These scholars studied Jurchen script and Chinese characters together.
Knowledge makes people more powerful — always true in any era.

scholar2-h1.title: 学者的笔记
trans: Jin Dynasty had a hard-working scholar who read many books every day.
He wrote everything he learned in his notebook.
He studied history, literature, and philosophy — very knowledgeable.
His notes were treated as precious materials by later scholars.
His story tells us: study diligently, and knowledge is power.

shang-h1.title: 骨头上的字

sents.mn: to know; to become aware of

trans: Long ago, China had a dynasty called the Shang.
Shang Dynasty people wrote characters on bones.
The bones were big, and many characters could be written on them.
They used these characters to ask the gods: "Will today be good?"
They wanted to know whether the weather would be good.
These are China's earliest characters.
The characters are small and beautiful.
One character is one thing, and it looks beautiful.
Later, people found these bones in the ground.
Today, we can still see these characters.

shang2-h1.title: 市场的一天
trans: Today is market day.
In the morning there are many people at the market.
Some people sell fruit; some people sell fish.
Some people also sell vegetables and meat.
I bought three apples — very delicious.
The apples were red, three yuan each.
Mum bought many things.
She bought fish, vegetables and fruit.
There were too many things, so I helped her carry them.
We went home together to eat.

shufa-h1.title: 写字高手
trans: Western Jin had a very famous person named Wang Xizhi.
He began learning to write when he was very young.
He practiced writing every day, never stopping.
He washed his brush after writing, until the water turned black.
His characters were written extremely beautifully.
People called him the "Sage of Calligraphy" — a saint of writing.
He and his friends wrote very famous characters in the mountains.
People still look at those characters today.
People in later times all wanted to learn his hand.
Today, people still learn his method of writing.

shufa2-h1.title: 学写汉字
trans: I started learning to write Chinese characters.
The teacher taught me how to hold a pen.
She said that if you sit up straight, your characters look better.
I practiced writing "water" and "mountain" many times.
A character has many strokes, and which one comes first matters.
At first my writing wasn't good, but slowly it got better.
The teacher looked and said: "Better than yesterday."
I showed the finished characters to my mother.
She said they looked lovely and put them up in her room.
Now I love writing Chinese characters; every character is beautiful.

song-h1.title: 中国的四大发明
trans: Song Dynasty people invented movable-type printing.
This made books cheap, and more people could read.
Chinese people also invented gunpowder, the compass, and paper-making.
The compass helped sailors find their direction at sea.
These inventions changed the whole world.

song2-h1.title: 纸钱的魔力
trans: During the Song Dynasty, people invented paper money.
Before, people used heavy copper coins for trading.
With paper money, merchants could trade more conveniently.
This invention made commerce even more developed.
The invention of paper money changed people's economic life.

tang-h1.title: 长安的繁华
trans: The Tang capital Chang'an was the world's largest city at that time.
Merchants from different countries came here to do business.
The great poet Li Bai wrote many beautiful poems.
At that time, women could ride horses, study, and live freely.
The Tang Dynasty was one of China's most glorious eras.

tang2-h1.title: 诗人看月亮
tang2-h1.en: The Poet Looks at the Moon
trans: The great Tang poet Li Bai loved watching the moon.
He drank wine alone, watching the moon in the night sky.
He missed his family far away; his heart felt very sad.
He wrote the famous poem: "Before my bed the bright moonlight gleams — I thought it was frost on the ground."
This poem brought comfort to many people away from home.

tao-h1.title: 田里的诗人

sents.mn: to like; to be fond of

trans: Eastern Jin had a poet who loved working in the fields.
He had once been an official.
But he did not like that kind of life.
He didn't want to be a big official — he only loved nature.
Later he went home, farmed his land and wrote poems.
He grew flowers and vegetables, happy every day.
In the morning he went to the fields; in the evening he wrote.
He wrote poems saying: "In the fields, my heart feels free."
His family was not rich, but he was happy.
His poems are beautiful; all Chinese people love him.

tao2-h1.title: 下雨天

sents.mn: outside (also pr. [wài mian] for this sense)

trans: Today it's raining; I cannot go out to play.
In the morning I saw that the sky was very dark.
I sat by the window and watched the rain outside.
The rain hitting the ground makes a nice sound.
Everyone on the road was walking quickly.
I decided to read books at home and drink hot tea.
Mum read at home too.
In the afternoon the rain slowly eased.
The sky brightened and everything outside looked clean.
Rainy days have their beautiful aspects too.

tea-h1.title: 一杯好茶
trans: Southern Song people extremely loved drinking tea.
They turned tea-drinking into an art form.
Teahouses were places where people met and chatted.
Good tea needs clean water and the correct temperature.
Today, drinking tea is still an important part of Chinese culture.

tea2-h1.title: 茶馆的故事
trans: During the Southern Song, Lin'an City had many famous teahouses.
People chatted, drank tea, and shared news in teahouses.
Artists performed in teahouses, telling stories to guests.
Teahouses were not just places to drink tea — they were cultural exchange centres.
Today, we can still see this kind of traditional teahouse culture.

xia-h1.title: 大禹治水
trans: Long ago, the waters of China were very high.
The water was very big; many people had no home.
Dayu was a good person.
The king asked him to look at the water and find a way.
Dayu went to work on the mountains.
He worked together with many people, and it was hard.
He did not return home for thirty years.
Three times he came to his own door and did not go in.
Later the water went down and people went home.
All Chinese people said Dayu was very good.

xia2-h1.title: 小龙学游泳
trans: There was a little dragon who couldn't swim.
Every day it watched the other dragons playing in the water.
It went into the river; the water was very big and cold.
It did not want to go in; it only wanted to watch the others swim.
Its mother said: "You can do it! Come!"
Mother said: "Watch me first — I will teach you."
The little dragon tried once, twice, three times.
The little dragon swam for a long time and learned.
Mother said: "You did very well."
Today, the little dragon is very happy in the water.

yuan-h1.title: 马可·波罗来华
trans: During the Yuan Dynasty, Kublai Khan ruled the world's largest empire.
Marco Polo came from Italy to China and lived in Dadu (Beijing) for 17 years.
He was extremely astonished by China's prosperity.
After returning to Europe, he wrote his experiences into a book.
This book let Europeans understand the wonderful world of the East for the first time.

yuan2-h1.title: 元朝的美食
trans: During the Yuan Dynasty, the Mongols brought many foods from different places.
Cheese, lamb, and milk tea became popular foods in the north.
Spices from Central Asia made Chinese cooking even more diverse.
Marco Polo recorded the various delicacies he tasted in China.
Food exchange between different cultures enriched Chinese food culture.

zhou-h1.title: 天命的故事
trans: After the Shang, China had the Western Zhou.
The Western Zhou king said: "Heaven lets me be king."
He said that Heaven watches every king.
The king must love the people; the people must also love the king.
If a king does well, Heaven lets him stay king.
If a king does badly, Heaven no longer allows it.
The king had many good soldiers.
They trained in the mountains every day.
People worked in the fields, and there was rice and meat at home.
At that time, China was very big and beautiful.

zhou2-h1.title: 大树下的朋友
trans: There is a big tree at the school gate.
That tree is very tall and very old.
My friends and I play under the big tree every day.
When the weather is nice, we read under the tree.
We play games, tell stories, and are very happy.
My friend can tell many lovely stories.
Today he told a very long story.
The teacher came and said: "Time for class!"
We all said: "Goodbye, big tree!"
We ran into the classroom and started studying.
